$comment: [OURS: the list is our own. INTENT.md 'Wording rules' and CLAUDE.md rule 8 give the constraint — describe episodes and behaviours, never dispositions, and never compare to other students — and docs/SPEC-gate0.md §9.2 names the three categories this list must cover. The evidence behind the constraint is docs/03-open-learner-models.md, which is cited by CLAUDE.md but is not in the repo. Nothing here is taken from a source paper. Each group carries the one-line reason it exists; someone will argue with an entry one day and should be able to see why it is there.]
$matching: Word-boundary, case-insensitive, whitespace between words is flexible. A group's `allow` list holds literal contexts where the group's phrases are copy we need; a match inside one of those is not reported. When in doubt the checker fires: a false positive costs one rewrite, a false negative ships a claim about a child.

groups.reason: A noun phrase naming a kind of student is a claim about the person; what this repo measures is the episode structure of a session (INTENT.md, 'What is measured').
groups.suggestion: Make the session or the work the subject: 'in this session the work moved from exploring to planning twice'.
groups.$note_allow: Owner decision D-C, 2026-09-18: the Student Report may say 'This stretch of <kind of work> opened on the student's turn.' with the stretch as the subject, and only that construction. Nothing wider is allowed: 'the student's turn' elsewhere still fires. The apostrophe is the straight one; a typographic one does not match and fires.
groups.$note_the_student: 'the student' fires in internal views too (the annotation interface, the agreement view). Use the role label 'Student' on a turn, or name the session. This list is for our copy; do not point the lint at codebook definitions, which are source text and say 'the student' where the paper did.

groups.reason: Ability talk names a trait rather than an episode, and trait feedback is what INTENT.md's wording rules exist to keep out of the report.
groups.suggestion: Drop the trait. Say what kind of work happened, when in the session, and for how long.

groups.reason: No comparison to other students, including an implicit one (INTENT.md 'Wording rules'; docs/SPEC-gate0.md §9.2 names typical, average, on track, ahead, behind).
groups.suggestion: Compare the sessions to each other, or give the number: 'episodes ran 6 to 14 turns'.
groups.$note_allow: CLAUDE.md rule 7 requires an evidence link to the turns behind every claim, so 'the turns behind this claim' is copy the product needs.

groups.reason: Whether the student improved is on INTENT.md's not-measured list; the report claims process visibility, not learning gains.
groups.suggestion: Say what changed in the shape of the sessions: 'verification appears in four of the last five sessions'.
groups.$note_progress: 'progress' is word-boundary matched, so 'the progression of episodes' does not fire. 'progression' is deliberately absent.

groups.reason: INTENT.md: nothing framed as a deficit without something actionable attached, and no verdict on the work; a verdict on the session reads as a verdict on the child sitting next to the parent.
groups.suggestion: Describe the episode and link its turns. If there is nothing actionable to attach, leave it out.

groups.reason: These assert an absence no transcript shows and credit the student with it. Layer 2 observes one tutor turn before a boundary; a tutor who prompted earlier, paused or waited still shaped what followed (INTENT.md 'Layer 2'; CLAUDE.md rules 8 and 13).
groups.suggestion: Keep the stretch of work as the subject and say only what one turn shows: 'this stretch of planning opened on a Student turn'. Add ', with no prompt in the turn before it' only where Layer 2 codes that turn NONE and the layer surfaces.
